h1:
🌶️ Best Michelin Southern Thai
Southern Thai in the Michelin Guide
intro: Southern Thai is the boldest flavor in the whole guide: chili-hot, salty, loud with turmeric and shrimp paste. It is led by Sorn, Thailand's only three-star southern kitchen, whose twenty-plus-course tasting menu is built around a southern crab curry. Below it sit Bib Gourmand favorites like The Charm Dining Gallery, whose Baba-Phuket moo hong the inspectors singled out, and Mor Mu Dong, famous for a whole mackerel deboned and restuffed with seasoned fish.
quickAnswerHtml: 23 southern Thai restaurants in the Michelin Guide Thailand 2026, led by Sorn, the three-star kitchen whose tasting menu centers on a rich southern crab curry.

blocks.html: Southern Thai is the boldest flavor in the whole guide: chili-hot, salty, loud with turmeric and shrimp paste. It is led by Sorn, Thailand's only three-star southern kitchen, whose twenty-plus-course tasting menu is built around a southern crab curry. Below it sit Bib Gourmand favorites like The Charm Dining Gallery, whose Baba-Phuket moo hong the inspectors singled out, and Mor Mu Dong, famous for a whole mackerel deboned and restuffed with seasoned fish.

blocks.name: Sorn
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per person is THB 7,800++ for the regular tasting menu; once you add service charge and tax, prepare around THB 9,180 per person, and full payment is required at the time of booking. The key condition to know before you book is that there are no refunds, reschedules, or cancellations of any kind. Arriving more than 30 minutes late means you forfeit your table, and the kitchen cannot accommodate shellfish allergies or vegetarian/vegan diets.

There are two doors to booking. The first, for everyone, is TableCheck, which opens booking for the following month at noon Bangkok time on the 25th of every month (moved to the 24th if the 25th falls on a Saturday). There are only about 22 seats, so you need to click the instant it opens. The second door, for international guests, is the email reservation@sornfinesouthern.com from midnight Bangkok time on the 15th, or call +66 99 081 1119. The restaurant serves dinner only from 18:00 (the official Instagram lists Sunday–Friday, closed Saturday — double-check the exact seating times on TableCheck). To get there, take the BTS to Phrom Phong then walk into Sukhumvit Soi 26 for about 15 minutes; if you're driving, you can park at the Four Wings Hotel for THB 50/hour, with a free shuttle to the restaurant. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Southern crab curry, part of a Southern Thai tasting menu of more than 20 courses
blocks.bestFor: A major celebration meal for Southern Thai food lovers who are ready to race the clock to book weeks ahead
blocks.hours: Dinner only, from 18:00; official Instagram bio lists servic

blocks.name: Baan Suan Lung Khai
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Suan Lung Khai sits on Round-Island Road Route 4170 in Ban Taling Ngam, on the south side of Koh Samui, about a 40-minute drive from Chaweng Beach and close to the Virgin Coast side and the island's sunset viewpoints. The restaurant is open every day in two seatings, 11:00–14:00 and 16:30–19:30, but only for guests who have booked ahead — walk-ins are not accepted at all, since Lung Khai prepares ingredients based on each day's reservation count. You need to call at least 1 day ahead at 098-015-2845 or 083-984-5629 (Wongnai notes LINE booking is also available). During high season, Dec–Feb, book several days ahead.

Pricing is a set menu per person, with 4 price tiers to choose from: 350, 500, 700, or 1,000 baht. When you book, let them know your headcount and budget, and the kitchen will put together a meal based on that day's fresh ingredients. Dress is casual, since you're eating out in a coconut grove. The recommended time is the evening seating at 16:30, so you finish in time to head to the sunset viewpoint on the Taling Ngam side right after. The daytime seating suits anyone staying on the south side or doing an island driving loop. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Southern seafood set — picked blue swimmer crab and grilled prawns, served on a woven tray under a dome cover
mustOrder: Southern seafood set (picked blue swimmer crab, grilled prawns)
Pandan coconut rice on a woven tray under a dome cover
Traditional local sweets to close the set
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants Southern Thai seafood from local fishermen in a coconut grove on Samui's south side, ready to book ahead
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Baan Suan Lung Khai official Facebook page

blocks.name: Beer Hima (Chatuchak)
blocks.descHtml:
Budget is typically around THB 500–1,000 per head, but if you order fresh seafood from the tanks, which is priced by weight, a large group's bill can climb into the thousands per person. The restaurant is open daily 11:00–23:00. Book by calling directly at 02-954-3404 or 02-954-3405 — the restaurant manages its own queue, not through any app — or just walk in, since it's a large restaurant with multiple rooms. Real waits only happen during busy weekend dinners. If you're coming as a large group, it's worth calling ahead to book the private room, which seats up to 30.

The restaurant is in the Chatuchak/Prachachuen area, on Thetsaban Songkhro Rd, not near any train line. Driving is the most convenient option since the restaurant has its own car park, or a ride from the city centre isn't far either. The best time to go is early evening, when you get the best pick of fresh seafood from the tanks while avoiding the peak crowd. Visa, Mastercard, JCB, and UnionPay are all accepted. Read the full review →
mustOrder: Stir-fried prawns with shrimp paste and bitter beans
blocks.bestFor: Family meals and big groups who love Southern Thai food and fresh seafood — a private room for 30, its own car park, no queue anxiety

blocks.name: Jaan by Khun Jim
blocks.descHtml:
Budget is the first reason to go — dishes here run just 99-300 baht, averaging around 250-500 baht a head for a full meal. Booking works only one way: call directly at 063-924-2597 or message the restaurant's Facebook page, since the restaurant handles all its own bookings and there's no online platform to book through. Since winning the Bib Gourmand in 2026, it's noticeably busier, so if you're planning a dinner or weekend visit, call at least a day or two ahead to be safe.

The restaurant is open daily 11:00-21:00, located on Soi Chan 7 in the Sathon Tai area. If you're using public transport, get off at BRT Thanon Chan station and walk about 10 minutes; driving yourself is even easier since the restaurant has its own parking. Payment accepts both Visa and Mastercard credit cards. The best time to go is a weekday lunch, when you can still walk in without trouble. There's no dress code — it's a two-storey house in a garden, and you can sit down and eat like family. Read the full review →
blocks.cuisine: Southern Thai food with Teochew Chinese roots (Trang style)
blocks.signature: Trang-style crushed fresh shrimp chilli paste, finished with fresh coconut milk sago at 99 baht a plate
blocks.bestFor: Family meals and anyone who wants real Trang-style Southern Thai food on a budget of a few hundred baht
blocks.foodType: Southern Thai food with Teochew Chinese roots (Trang style)
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Jaan by Khun Jim official Instagram (@jaanbykhunjim)

blocks.name: Janhom
blocks.descHtml:
Janhom is one of the easiest Bib Gourmand Southern Thai restaurants to visit, because walk-ins are the normal way to go — the restaurant has no online booking platform at all. If you're going as a big group and want to be sure of a table, call ahead at 02-319-1128 or 02-319-1129. The budget is easy on the wallet, around THB 150–250 a dish (kaeng tai pla 180, kaeng som pla ka 222, sataw pad kapi kung 245), working out to about THB 250–500 a head. Credit cards are accepted with a THB 500 minimum.

The restaurant sits on Soi Ramkhamhaeng 21 (Soi Nawasri) in Wang Thonglang, with no BTS/MRT station nearby — driving is the most convenient option since the restaurant has its own parking, or you can grab a taxi/ride-hailing app straight into the soi. It's open daily from roughly 10:00–21:00, though some older sources list it as closed on Mondays — worth a call ahead to be sure. The time to avoid is weekday lunch 12:00–13:00, when local office workers pack the place and you may have to wait for a table; going before 11:30 or from around 13:30 onward means comfortable seating. If getting there isn't convenient, you can also order through LINE MAN, though the turmeric-fried dishes taste far better fresh at the restaurant. Read the full review →
blocks.bestFor: Family meals/groups of friends who want real bold-flavoured Southern Thai food for under 500 baht a head, with no need to book ahead
blocks.hours: Daily ~10:00–21:00 (Wongnai; some older sources list it as closed Mondays

blocks.name: Jun Hom
blocks.descHtml:
Jun Hom sits on Mae Nam–Bang Po beach, on the north side of Koh Samui, Surat Thani province. Budget runs around 250–500 THB per person, and the plates come large enough to share, so the more people you bring the better the value. Open every day — Wongnai lists 10:00–22:00, while the Koh Samui municipal website lists 11:00–21:00 — so if you're planning an early or late visit, it's worth calling ahead to check at 077-236-458 or 077-602-008. The restaurant is mainly walk-in, but MICHELIN notes the restaurant handles bookings itself by phone, which is worth using if you're going in the evening, since it's open-air right on the beach with limited tables and a kitchen that cooks one dish at a time — tables fill up around sunset, so budget extra time for your food to arrive.

Getting there means driving a car or rented motorbike along the ring road on the island's north side; the Mae Nam/Bang Po zone sits along the route from Na Thon pier toward Bo Phut beach, with no regular public transport. The best time to go is late afternoon before 5pm, to grab a seaside table before the crowds arrive, or a relaxed lunch when tables are easy to find. Dress is casual — there's no dress code. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fried lek khon fish, a local Samui fish hard to find off the island
mustOrder: Fried lek khon fish (local Samui fish)
blocks.bestFor: A big shared seafood meal by the sea with friends or family, best at sunset on Samui's north side
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Jun Hom Seafood Koh Samui official Facebook page

blocks.name: Kin-Kub-Ei
blocks.descHtml:
Kin-Kub-Ei is booking-only — it does not accept walk-ins at all. Book through Facebook Messenger (the eatwithaunt page) or LINE @kinkubei, or call 083-509-8264. There's a 500 THB booking deposit, since the restaurant cooks only for the number of guests booked. On weekends, message well in advance since seats fill up fast. The restaurant is open Wednesday to Sunday, 11:00–17:00, closed Monday and Tuesday, and you should reconfirm the seating time when you book.

On budget, main dishes run around 290–300 THB, averaging about 300–600 THB per person — great value for Bib Gourmand-level food. The restaurant has parking and takes credit cards. It sits on Si Sunthon Road, Si Sunthon subdistrict, Thalang district, in the middle of Phuket island near the Thao Thep Kasattri–Thao Sri Sunthon monument. The easiest way there is by car or private ride — it's not far south of Phuket airport, making it a good lunch stop before heading into town or on the way to the west-coast beaches. Must-order dishes are the fried fish with curry paste sauce, moo hong, stir-fried squid in black ink, and nam chup yoh. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fried fish with curry paste sauce
mustOrder: Fried fish with curry paste sauce
blocks.bestFor: Real home-style southern Thai cooking in Phuket, for travelers who plan ahead and want a home-cooked meal rather than a typical restaurant experience

blocks.name: Krua Baan Platong
mustOrder: Steamed pork belly with budu dipping sauce
Gaeng som with mong fish and chon
blocks.bestFor: For anyone who wants real Phuket home-cooked food and can plan 2–3 days ahead

blocks.name: Krua Kao Kuk
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Kao Kuk is in the Talat Nuea area of Phuket Town, near the Thanon Phattana intersection, not far from the old town — you can drive or take a songthaew there easily from the old town area, and the shop has its own parking, which is fairly rare for a shop in Phuket Town. Open every day 11:30–20:30, no closing days, and prices are very friendly for a Bib Gourmand-level shop — around THB 60–300 per dish (MICHELIN price rating ฿฿). Two people can eat a full spread on a budget of THB 300–500.

The shop takes walk-ins only, no online booking, but if you want to check whether it's open or whether a dish has sold out, you can call ahead at 087-569-7574. The key thing to know before you go: the shop accepts cash only, according to MICHELIN. So bring cash with you. The recommended times are lunch right after opening around 11:30am, when everything is still available, or dinner between 5 and 6pm before locals arrive after work. If you're coming in the evening, don't arrive later than 7:30pm, since the shop closes at 8:30pm and standout dishes like the fish porridge may sell out first. Dress is casual — this is a true local porridge shop. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Hakka-Phuket-style fish porridge, Amah's original Peranakan recipe
mustOrder: Crab omelette packed with crab meat
blocks.bestFor: Fans of genuine local Phuket food, families, and old-town visitors who want to close out the day with an original-recipe fish porridge at a wallet-friendly price
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Krua Kao Kuk official Facebook page

blocks.name: Krua Luang Ten
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Luang Ten sits on Phetkasem Road in Khao Lak (Khuek Khak subdistrict), across from the entrance to Laem Pakarang — drive straight in along Phetkasem Road from Phang-Nga town or Phuket airport. Prices are gentle for a MICHELIN restaurant — most dishes run around 80–120 THB, so a budget of about 250–500 THB per person covers several dishes. The restaurant opens for two sessions, lunch roughly 11:00–13:30 and dinner roughly 17:00–20:00 (some sources, including MICHELIN, list closing as late as 21:30 — call ahead to confirm). One thing to remember firmly: the restaurant closes every 10th, 20th, and 30th of the month — don't drive out on those days.

The restaurant is mainly walk-in. If you want to be sure, call the restaurant directly at +66 90 716 4182. Lunch service gets very busy and the kitchen closes early (13:30) — arrive before 11:30 to beat the crowd, or go for dinner instead. Key tip: the restaurant takes your order only once, so decide your full menu before calling the server over. Dress is casual, and you can sit right down at the sand-floor tables. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Coconut curry with hed craeng mushroom and sator beans
mustOrder: Coconut curry with hed craeng mushroom and sator beans
Woi wai pad yanat sai kapi (stir-fried mantis shrimp with pineapple)
Raw vegetables with fermented fish sauce dip (free)
blocks.bestFor: Bold, authentic Southern Thai food for families/friend groups staying in Khao Lak, drivers touring Phang-Nga who want MICHELIN food on a light budget

blocks.name: Krua Praya
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Praya is on Soi Hua Tha 1 in the Si Sunthon area of Thalang district, near the Thao Thep Kasattri-Thao Sri Sunthon Monument — easy to drive to, with its own parking lot and wheelchair-accessible entrance. Open 11:00–22:00, closed every Tuesday. Prices run around 50–400 THB per dish (฿฿ level per MICHELIN); come with 3–4 people, order enough dishes to cover the table, and it still works out to about a hundred baht or so per head. Credit cards accepted, including Visa, Mastercard, and JCB.

The restaurant takes bookings by phone directly at 083-138-6789 — there's no online booking system. On weekday lunches you can simply walk in, but weekend evenings get the busiest, so it's worth calling ahead. The restaurant itself is a large, old-style Thai house with both an indoor zone and an outdoor zone, comfortably handling big groups — pick whichever suits the weather that day. The location sits in the middle of the island, closer to Phuket Airport than to the town center, making it a good pick for a first meal after landing or a final meal before flying out. Check the restaurant's Facebook page for menu updates and any special closures. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Stir-fried crispy pork belly with curry paste and young coconut shoots
mustOrder: Stir-fried crispy pork belly with curry paste and young coconut shoots
Crab meat curry in coconut milk
blocks.bestFor: A family or group meal for real spicy Phuket-style Southern food in a traditional Thai house, local prices, near the heroines' monument
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Krua Praya official Facebook page

blocks.name: Lucky
mustOrder: Sour curry with coconut shoot and sea bass
blocks.bestFor: A family meal or a meal for guests in downtown Surat Thani, or a Southern Thai meal before the boat to Samui-Phangan

blocks.name: Mor Mu Dong
blocks.descHtml:
Mor Mu Dong is walk-in only, no reservations — first come, first seated. There's a phone number for questions at 088-766-1634. Open daily 10:00–21:30, but there's one important rule to remember: the restaurant closes on the 15th of every month, and if the 15th falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the closure shifts to the following Monday instead. Worth checking the calendar before you leave your hotel so you don't waste a trip. Budget runs around 300–500 THB per person — very light for Bib Gourmand-level seafood. On payment, sources still disagree on whether cards are accepted, so bringing cash is the safest bet.

Getting there requires driving or hiring a ride — the restaurant sits in the mangroves along Mu Dong canal, off Soi Pa Lai from Chao Fah East Road, in the Chalong zone, near the old Phuket Zoo. The best time to go is before noon, since the wooden canal-side pavilions are limited — arrive early for the best spot with the best view. If you're set on the salt-grilled fish, order it the moment you sit down since it takes about 30 minutes on the grill. Dress code is casual. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Stuffed mackerel — boned whole, then stuffed back with seasoned minced fish into the fish skin
blocks.bestFor: For real Southern seafood fans who want to escape the chaos of Phuket's beach side, sitting in a wooden pavilion in the mangroves by the canal

blocks.name: Mun
blocks.descHtml:
Mun Phochana sits along Phetkasem Road in Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang district, Phang-Nga, on the route to Thap Lamu Pier where boats leave for the Similan Islands — your own car is the most convenient way to get there. The restaurant is open daily 10:00–22:30 (per MICHELIN's listing), and you don't need to book ahead since it's walk-in only, but if you want to check ahead or are coming as a large group, you can call +66 99 953 5422, which the restaurant handles directly. One important thing to know: it's cash only per MICHELIN's listing, so bring enough bills.

Budget runs about 101–250 THB per head, which is quite light for a Bib Gourmand-level restaurant, though loading up on several seafood dishes can push it to around 500 THB per person. Evenings tend to get busy with divers stopping by on their way back from Similan, so if you'd rather avoid the crowd, come in the afternoon or for lunch instead — easy to do since the restaurant stays open all day. Dishes to order are the stir-fried crab with lime, the curry with pond snails and wild betel leaf, and whatever fresh seafood from local fishing boats is available that day. Read the full review →
mustOrder: Curry with pond snails and wild betel leaf
Fresh seafood from local fishing boats
blocks.bestFor: Divers returning from Similan · seafood-loving families · budget MICHELIN trail-followers

blocks.name: Naam Yoi
blocks.descHtml:
Naam Yoi is on Ruam Phatthana Road, Rassada subdistrict, on the edge of Phuket Town, about a 10-minute drive from Phuket's old town district. Open daily 10:30–14:30 and 16:30–19:30 (some sources note it closes for an afternoon break from 14:00, so allow a little buffer). Prices sit at THB-THB, MICHELIN's price tier — realistically just a few hundred baht per person — but bring cash, since the restaurant is cash-only.

The restaurant runs mainly on walk-ins. If you want to book a table ahead, phone reservations are taken Monday–Friday only, at 076-525-858 or 099-629-3656. Tables are limited and dishes are cooked fresh to order from ingredients bought before dawn, so the best items sell out fast. Go before the lunch rush — arriving between 10:30–11:30 gets you the full menu. There's no English menu, so if you're going with foreign friends, it helps to have the Thai dish names ready, such as moo hong, gaeng som pla sod, and fried sand goby fish with turmeric. Read the full review →
mustOrder: Gaeng som pla sod (sour fish curry, house-made chili paste)
Fried sand goby fish with turmeric
Prawns stir-fried with shrimp paste and sator
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants original-recipe Phuket local food the way locals actually eat it, not the tourist version

faq.q: Which southern Thai restaurant is the best in the guide?
faq.a: Sorn in Bangkok is the sole three-star southern kitchen, serving a twenty-plus-course tasting menu built around its southern crab curry. If you want southern flavor pushed to its limit, this is the one.

faq.q: Where can I eat southern Thai on a budget?
faq.a: The Bib Gourmand picks are the best value. Jaan by Khun Jim serves a Trang-style fresh shrimp nam prik and coconut sago at 99 baht a plate, while Beer Hima is known for its yellow curry with grouper.

faq.q: What southern dishes should I order?
faq.a: Try the gaeng tai pla fish-innards curry at Janhom, yellow grouper curry at Beer Hima, moo hong braised pork at The Charm Dining Gallery and One Chun, and the stuffed mackerel at Mor Mu Dong. All are hard-to-find, genuinely southern plates.

faq.q: Where should I eat southern Thai in Phuket?
faq.a: Phuket has the most southern Bib Gourmand picks in this group. One Chun is known for moo hong and crab curry with wild betel leaf and rice noodles, Mor Mu Dong for its stuffed mackerel, and Krua Kao Kuk for Hakka-Phuket fish congee from a Peranakan grandmother's recipe.

faq.q: Which restaurants should I book ahead?
faq.a: Sorn requires advance booking and fills up fast as a three-star tasting menu. Bib Gourmand spots like One Chun in Phuket and Baan Suan Lung Khai in Surat Thani get busy on weekends, so calling ahead is the safer bet.
